test_title: PYST 10: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - Reasoning (Held On: 12 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: reasoning
question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

All cars are buses.

Some cars are trucks.

Conclusions (I): Some trucks are cars.

Conclusions (II): Some buses are cars.
solution:
Given Statements:

All cars are buses.

Some cars are trucks.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/018e302c23acc3ee5ca98e71214217fbb40d6555d6d5e2c56b8b44f38853a627.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d60c63dd01cca40d2a704d92a5be3aeb396c82daa5bbae3079985dde28808a38.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some trucks are cars.

If there is an intersection between set A (Cars) and set C (Trucks), then it is always true that Some C are A.

Therefore, conclusion (I) logically follows.

II. Some buses are cars.

The statement All A are B always implies that Some B are A. (Since all cars are buses, the set of buses must contain the set of cars, meaning some members of the 'Buses' set are also 'Cars').

Therefore, conclusion (II) logically follows.

So, Both conclusions (I) and (II) follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
